title: Relation-component topology predicts microrecord unit boundaries
summary: GDT701 finds seven singleton components, one fan-out and one serial chain. A speculative functional hypothesis is that connected-component topology, not line proximity, determines the smallest process-record unit.

design.unit: connected occurrence-node component containing admitted relation edges
design.contrast: graph component is one process unit versus line/page proximity defines the unit
design.prediction: Held components should preserve internal participant continuity and isolate from neighboring actions; singleton, fan-out, and serial topologies should predict distinct unit signatures.
design.countermodel: The graph may reflect sparse surviving evidence while the true record unit follows paragraph or line boundaries independently.
design.falsifier: A held component crosses an independently observed record boundary without continuity, or adjacent unconnected edges form the same process unit more often than connected components do.
design.principal_risk: Current graph edges are occurrence-bound and sparse; no broad record semantics or translation follows from topology alone.
design.related: Near GDT697/GDT701 and the closed relation-edge capacity routes, but proposes a unit-boundary rule rather than a new edge or word meaning.

source_evidence.quote:
- 11/11 inherited edges assigned exactly once to 9 components.
- 7 one-edge components, 1 repeated-destination fan-out, 1 serial chain.
- 23 edge nodes, 25 incidences, 25 minimal-hull positions, 2 hull-only
  positions and 1 render-only structural position.
- 17 held rivals and 27 reference decisions preserved unchanged.
- 479 token glosses, 51 line translations and 3 bound spans byte-identical.
